result.oneSentenceSummary: add_members raises RecordNotUnique for existing or duplicate usernames
result.improvedCode:
def add_members
    group = Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)
    usernames = params.require(:usernames)

    return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic

    Group.transaction do
      existing_user_ids = group.user_ids.to_set

      usernames.split(",").map(&:strip).reject(&:blank?).uniq.each do |username|
        user = User.find_by_username(username)
        next unless user
        next if existing_user_ids.include?(user.id)

        group.add(user)
        existing_user_ids << user.id
      end
    end

    if group.save
      render json: success_json
    else
      render_json_error(group)
    end
  end

judge.titleReason: The title names the core defect: add_members raises RecordNotUnique when a username is already a member or repeated, though it leaves out the missing transaction.

for i in range(num_queues):
            # Bound each queue so a burst of incoming messages blocks the
            # consumer (backpressure) instead of growing memory without limit.
            work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]] = queue.Queue(maxsize=1000)
            self.queues.append(work_queue)

            worker = OrderedQueueWorker[T](
                worker_id=i,
                work_queue=work_queue,
                result_processor=result_processor,
                identifier=identifier,
                offset_tracker=self.offset_tracker,
            )
            worker.start()
            self.workers.append(worker)

    def get_queue_for_group(self, group_key: str) -> int:
        """
        Get queue index for a group using consistent hashing.
        """
        return hash(group_key) % self.num_queues

    def submit(self, group_key: str, work_item: WorkItem[T]) -> None:
        """
        Submit a work item to the appropriate queue.

        Blocks while the target queue is full, applying backpressure to the
        caller until the worker catches up.
        """
        queue_index = self.get_queue_for_group(group_key)
        work_queue = self.queues[queue_index]

        self.offset_tracker.add_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
        work_queue.put(work_item, block=True)

judge.titleReason: The title names the defect: unbounded queues give no backpressure and can exhaust memory.
judge.fixReason: The fix bounds each queue with maxsize=1000 and uses a blocking put, so producers wait instead of dropping work; group assignment and FIFO order are unchanged, and add_offset still runs before put, so workers cannot complete an offset before it is registered.

result.oneSentenceSummary: Error upsampling misses count() with spacing or alias variants
result.improvedCode:
def transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(
    query_columns: Sequence[str],
) -> list[str]:
    """
    Transform aggregation functions to use sum(sample_weight) instead of count()
    for error upsampling. Only called when all projects are allowlisted.
    """
    import re

    count_pattern = re.compile(r"count\s*\(\s*\)(?:\s+as\s+(\w+))?", re.IGNORECASE)

    transformed_columns = []
    for column in query_columns:
        match = count_pattern.fullmatch(column.strip())

        if match:
            # Simple count becomes sum of sample weights, preserving any alias
            alias = match.group(1) or "count"
            transformed_columns.append(f"upsampled_count() as {alias}")

        else:
            transformed_columns.append(column)

    return transformed_columns

judge.titleReason: The title correctly states that error upsampling fails to recognize `count()` written with spacing or alias variants, which is the defect.
judge.fixReason: The case-insensitive regex fullmatch on the stripped column rewrites zero-argument counts that have inner whitespace or an explicit alias, keeps the alias's original case (defaulting to `count`), and appends every other column unchanged in its original order.
